newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower as funds sell 35 mln bushels.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower as funds sell 35 mln bushels.

text.p: CBOT corn ended lower as funds sold at least 35 million bushels, keying off a technical move below the 50-day moving average, traders said.
"We're under the 50-day moving average of $2.98-1/4 in the July," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co. "I think a lot of people were waiting for that."
Fundamentally, corn struggled all session, led by new crop December on ideas farmers would plant large amounts of corn this weekend and on lackluster USDA weekly export sales.
Cash sources said farmers were eager to get the crop into the ground this week.

Floor sources estimated corn plantings would by 20 to 30 percent complete as of Monday. USDA last Monday said corn plantings were seven percent complete as of Sunday, in line with the five-year average.

Traders and cash sources noted some farmers who waited for warmer weather last year instead faced a lengthy cool, wet spring that put corn plantings off to a late start and forced some farmers to switch intended corn acreage to soybeans.
Corn ended 5-1/2 to 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower with May down 5-1/2 cents at $2.93 a bushel and new crop December down 3-3/4 at $2.78-1/2.

But the National Weather Service Wednesday called for below normal temperatures and normal to above normal precipitation in the Midwest April 29 through May 3. That scenario could slow corn seeding progress, traders said.

USDA weekly corn export sales figures were said to be mediocre. USDA on Thursday pegged U.S. net export sales of corn for the week ended April 17 at 491,800 tonnes, near the low end of expectations for 400,000 tonnes.
Funds were aggressive sellers on the day, accounting for at least 35 million bushels in corn sales, traders said.

On the day, Griffin Trading sold 15 million bushels July corn, E.D. and F. Man International sold at least five million bushels May and four million December, Prudential Securities sold 4.5 million July and Refco Inc sold 3.5 million July and 3.0 million December, pit sources said.
Commercials were said to be buyers on the breaks. Cargill Inc bought two million bushels July and Continental Grain and Term Commodities were also buyers.
In spread trade, CIS spread 1.5 million bushels December/March at 4-1/2 cents, premium March, and LFG spread one million July/May at 1/2 to 3/4 cent, premium July.
In the options pit, Farmers Commodities Corp sold 600 July $2.90 calls at 15-1/2 to 15 cents, FIMAT Futures sold 1,300 July $2.90 puts at 7-1/2 to nine cents.
Corn volume was estimated by CBOT at 85,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 60,538 contracts.
